title: Type-Safe Financial Ledger Integration
business: A boutique fintech firm managing cross-border currency conversions.
problem: Runtime errors in JavaScript-based transaction processing logic frequently cause silent failures when handling unexpected currency record formats, leading to reconciliation discrepancies.
solution: PureScript provides algebraic data types and row polymorphism to strictly define transaction schemas, ensuring that any missing or malformed data in a ledger record is caught at compile-time rather than during execution.
steps: Define a sum type for Currency using algebraic data types to restrict valid inputs.
Implement a record type with row polymorphism to represent flexible ledger entries.
Write pure transformation functions that map incoming JSON to the validated record types.
Use the Effect monad to handle the side-effecting process of writing validated records to the database.
Compile the PureScript modules into clean JavaScript for integration with existing Node.js services.
outcome: The system achieves structural integrity where the application logic cannot proceed unless the transaction data strictly conforms to the defined financial schema, significantly reducing runtime exceptions.
limitation: The primary limitation is the increased cognitive load and compilation overhead associated with strict type checking; developers can verify this by monitoring the time taken for the Spago build tool to perform type inference on large, deeply nested record structures.

code.content:
data Currency = USD | EUR | GBP -- Algebraic data type for strict currency control
type LedgerEntry = { amount :: Number, currency :: Currency } -- Row polymorphism for record structure
processEntry :: LedgerEntry -> String
processEntry entry = "Processed " <> show entry.amount -- Pure function ensures data is valid before processing
code.explanation: This code demonstrates how algebraic data types and records enforce structure on financial data before any side effects occur.
